newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos tells Aquino he will step down in '98.
newsitem.headline: Ramos tells Aquino he will step down in '98.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos, seeking to quell speculation he would seek to prolong his time in power, told former president Corazon Aquino on Sunday he would step down at the end of his term in mid-1998.

"It's time for the others" to serve, a presidential palace news release quoted Ramos as saying at a luncheon he gave for Aquino and other former officials who took part in the 1986 popular revolt that ended Ferdinand Marcos's 20-year rule.
It was the fourth time in the past week that Ramos had made a public pledge to bow out of office when his six-year term ends in June next year.

Speculation that the former army general was interested in serving for another term was provoked by his own senior aides who said last week many members of the Lakas (People Power) administration party favoured amending the constitution to allow Ramos to stand for re-election.
They said they believed they could convince Ramos, credited for nourishing the country's economic rebirth, to agree.

The constitution, adopted in 1987, fixes the presidential term at six years without re-election. Its authors said the limitation was designed to prevent the rise of another authoritarian rule similar to that of Marcos.
Opposition and church groups have denounced the suggestion by Lakas party officials to extend Ramos's term, warning it could wreck Philippine democracy.
